1: # Architecture blueprint
2: 
3: Status: draft for human review. ADR-001 selects layout migration plus narrow
4: extensions; FR-A–D have not been implemented.
5: 
6: ## Drivers and boundaries
7: 
8: Preserve TradingAgents capabilities and Python imports; target Python 3.13; keep
9: four owners independent after interface approval; avoid new runtime dependencies;
10: require deterministic evidence and final-rating authority boundaries.
11: 
12: ```mermaid
13: flowchart LR
14:   CLI[CLI] --> Graph[Existing TradingAgents graph]
15:   Graph --> Sources[Existing dataflows and providers]
16:   Graph --> D[Planned deterministic eligibility gate D]
17:   D --> Reports[Authoritative result and reports]
18:   A[Planned dual-ticker comparison A] --> Graph
19:   B[Planned common-event grouping B] --> Sources
20:   Reports --> C[Planned manifest and query C]
21: ```
22: 
23: LLM narrative is advisory. Validated provider/evidence metadata and D's final
24: rating govern published structured results. Actual application guardrails remain
25: the upstream implementation until D is built and tested. INV-D is a target rule,
26: not an initialized enforcement claim. ADR-002 proposes an explicit `team`
27: decision mode and a deterministic graph node after the Portfolio Manager and
28: before publication; `standard` mode preserves existing behavior.
29: 
30: ## Components and integration
31: 
32: Upstream agents/graph/dataflows/llm_clients/memory/reporting and CLI retain their
33: responsibilities. Four planned modules are listed in AGENTS.md. Shared schema
34: proposals are in interface-contracts.md and require approval before implementation.
35: Default config and existing provider interfaces are reused.
36: 
37: ## Supervision, verification and observability
38: 
39: Prompt.md imposes human plan/test/build/verification gates. Project OpenCode
40: permissions use default-deny tool rules with explicit read scopes and per-edit
41: confirmation. Shell execution always requires confirmation; it is not an OS sandbox.
42: Three-tier verification follows verification-constraints.md. Results record real
43: commands and failures; PRs update trace links, reviews and AI-use metadata.
44: 
45: ## Change policy
46: 
47: Interface, dependency, safety and context-budget changes require ADR updates and
48: human review. Schema/model/prompt changes require relevant re-evaluation; a fixed
49: model evaluation runner/data remains a prerequisite for B delivery. No live API
50: calls, broker execution or remote repository modification are part of initialization.

(End of file - total 50 lines)
</content>

1: # ADR-002: deterministic team-mode decision eligibility gate
2: 
3: - Status: proposed; requires non-D safety review and approved D acceptance tests.
4: - Requirements: FR-D, NFR-D.
5: - Invariant: INV-D.
6: 
7: ## Context
8: 
9: The upstream Portfolio Manager supplies the candidate rating and narrative. The
10: existing verified-market-snapshot tool returns human-readable text for an agent;
11: that text is not a trustworthy machine interface for deciding whether a final
12: rating may be published. A model can also return an allowed rating when critical
13: market data was not executed, unavailable, missing, future-dated or stale. The
14: qualification boundary therefore needs deterministic evidence metadata and must
15: run before a final graph state can reach the CLI, reports or decision log.
16: 
17: ## Decision proposal
18: 
19: 1. Add an explicit `standard` / `team` decision mode. `standard` is the default
20:    and preserves the upstream path. Python graph callers can select
21:    `decision_mode="team"`; the CLI will expose `--decision-mode standard|team`.
22: 2. In team mode, track market-analyst selection and execution separately from
23:    market-evidence acquisition. A deterministic market-data adapter provides a
24:    status (`valid`, `unavailable`, `not_run`) and a canonical snapshot date; no
25:    status or date is inferred from model prose. Missing or malformed metadata
26:    fails closed.
27: 3. Reuse the upstream OHLCV stale-data policy (`MAX_OHLCV_STALE_DAYS`, currently
28:    10 calendar days). Reject a snapshot after the analysis date or older than
29:    this bound. This avoids creating a second freshness policy.
30: 4. Run a deterministic eligibility node after the Portfolio Manager and before
31:    graph completion. It accepts only the exact five allowed rating values. Any
32:    unmet condition sets authoritative `final_rating="REVIEW"`, emits ordered
33:    reason codes, and replaces public final-decision text with a review notice.
34:    The candidate's free-form Buy/Sell narrative is not exposed as the final
35:    decision when the gate rejects it.
36: 5. Keep `REVIEW` decisions out of pending settlement/reflection. Reports, CLI
37:    output and state logs use the gate's final rating and reasons. Non-critical
38:    analyst omissions continue following the existing runtime policy.
39: 
40: ## Alternatives considered
41: 
42: | Option | Assessment |
43: |---|---|
44: | Trust the market analyst's prose or ask another model to validate it | Rejected: model text cannot establish provider execution status or snapshot date. |
45: | Parse status/date back out of model-visible tool output | Rejected: couples enforcement to rendered text and makes evidence authority ambiguous. |
46: | Validate typed metadata with a deterministic graph node | Proposed: separates data provenance from narrative and places enforcement before publication. |
47: | Gate every upstream run by default | Rejected: silently changes existing callers and conflicts with the explicit team-mode boundary. |
48: 
49: ## Consequences and boundaries
50: 
51: - Team-mode graph, CLI, state and report adapters are coordinated integration
52:   changes and require review beyond the D-owned pure qualification module.
53: - The evidence adapter may use the existing cached OHLCV path; its test must
54:   prove that it does not accept rows beyond `trade_date` and that stale data
55:   follows the existing 10-day policy.
56: - A failed market-analyst subgraph must not leave an actionable result. The
57:   integration must either preserve other completed work with `REVIEW`, or fail
58:   closed without publishing a rating; the accepted test contract will determine
59:   the exact runtime failure representation.
60: - A `REVIEW` reason is machine-readable and user-visible. It must remain stable
61:   across CLI, Markdown, HTML and structured run-state output.
62: - Offline tests mock data and model clients; no live provider call is part of
63:   D's acceptance test suite.
64: 
65: ## Reconsider if
66: 
67: - Team requirements define another decision-mode interface or rating vocabulary.
68: - The upstream OHLCV stale policy changes or is unsuitable for the project.
69: - A structured upstream market-evidence API becomes available and removes the
70:   need for a team adapter.
71: - Review finds the proposed failure propagation or safe-report representation
72:   inadequate.

(End of file - total 72 lines)
</content>

1: # Interface contracts
2: 
3: Status: D contract proposal for test review; no D executable interface is claimed.
4: 
5: - A: exactly two distinct tickers, shared canonical date/config; sequentially call
6:   upstream propagate/save_reports, isolating each run. Return per-ticker status,
7:   rating, summary and report path, plus a comparison report.
8: - B: 2–3 tickers, window ≤7 days, ≤5 records per ticker. Each record contains a
9:   run-scoped evidence ID, ticker, published_at, source and title/snippet. Output
10:   groups reference input IDs; deterministic validation requires ≥2 tickers and
11:   correct provenance. At most one grouping call; no silent SDK retries in that cap.
12: - C: versioned manifest records run ID, ticker, date/as-of, start/end, available
13:   code version, configured providers/models/analysts, status and relative paths.
14:   Unknowns are explicit. Query is read-only and tolerates individual bad files.
15: - D: market execution status and snapshot date are machine metadata, not inferred
16:   from model text. The proposed public mode is `standard` (default; preserve
17:   upstream behavior) or `team` (apply the qualification gate). A team-mode run
18:   checks selected/actual market-analyst execution, independently verified
19:   market-evidence status, snapshot date and the exact five-tier final rating.
20:   Missing/unavailable/not-run/future/stale evidence or invalid rating yields
21:   authoritative `REVIEW` plus stable reason codes before any final state is
22:   streamed, reported or recorded for settlement. `REVIEW` is not queued for
23:   settlement/reflection. The existing OHLCV stale-data bound
24:   (`MAX_OHLCV_STALE_DAYS`, currently 10 calendar days) is the proposed freshness
25:   limit; D tests must pin the boundary and ADR-002 records this reuse.
26: 
27: ### D qualification boundary proposal
28: 
29: - Python callers select `decision_mode="team"` on `TradingAgentsGraph`; the CLI
30:   exposes `--decision-mode standard|team`, defaulting to `standard` for upstream
31:   compatibility. The mode and selected analysts are run metadata.
32: - Evidence acquisition returns typed metadata (`valid`, `unavailable`, or
33:   `not_run`) and a canonical `snapshot_date` when valid. Market-analyst execution
34:   status is a separate field. It uses deterministic market-data code, not a
35:   model-generated report. An absent evidence object, unknown status,
36:   missing/malformed date, date after `trade_date`, or data older than the
37:   existing 10-calendar-day OHLCV freshness bound fails closed.
38: - A deterministic graph node runs after the Portfolio Manager and before graph
39:   completion/publication. It writes authoritative `final_rating`, eligibility
40:   status and ordered reason codes. Ineligible output replaces the public final
41:   decision text with a `REVIEW` notice; model candidate prose cannot remain the
42:   apparent final call. Standard mode passes through the existing flow.
43: - Team-mode final state exposes `market_analyst_status`,
44:   `market_evidence_status`, `snapshot_date` and `eligibility_reason_codes`.
45:   The reason list is empty on an eligible result. Public graph stream frames
46:   and CLI live decision panels only publish a final rating after qualification.
47: - Initial reason-code proposal (report all applicable causes in this order):
48:   `market_analyst_not_run`, `market_analyst_failed`,
49:   `market_analyst_invalid_status`,
50:   `market_evidence_missing`, `market_evidence_not_run`,
51:   `market_evidence_unavailable`, `market_evidence_invalid_status`,
52:   `market_snapshot_date_missing`, `market_snapshot_date_invalid`,
53:   `market_snapshot_after_analysis`, `market_snapshot_stale`,
54:   `analysis_date_invalid`, and `invalid_rating`. The D test plan fixes their expected mappings before
55:   implementation.
56: 
57: Use UTC-aware stored timestamps; analysis dates remain explicit trading dates.
58: Freeze schema, null semantics, identifiers and errors before parallel coding.
59: Reserve `test/offline/test_comparison.py`, `test_events.py`, `test_manifest.py`,
60: `test_eligibility.py` for owners A, B, C, D respectively. Shared CLI/graph/report
61: files require coordinated integration PRs; no direct private cross-module imports.

(End of file - total 61 lines)
</content>

1: # Verification constraints
2: 
3: Every fit criterion has a test; every invariant has a violation-triggered failing
4: test. New tests name requirement/invariant IDs. Feature tests must be approved
5: before implementation. Keep expected outcomes independent of production logic.
6: Modules A–D follow the same [GitHub Flow](../testing/test-approval-process.md):
7: record test evidence on the draft PR before application code, run all offline
8: tests locally and in CI, and require independent final review before merging.
9: 
10: 1. Structural: package/CLI imports, resource discovery, dependency/module boundary,
11:    permissions and requirement schema validation.
12: 2. Regression: all previously established offline suites must pass each round.
13: 3. Behavioral: frozen evidence-ID, REVIEW safety, recovery, timing and semantic
14:    grouping thresholds. Mock model output tests cannot prove real model quality.
15: 
16: B needs at least 20 human-labeled news pairs (10 positive/10 negative), pairwise
17: precision ≥0.80 and recall ≥0.70 under the approved model/evaluation procedure.
18: The evaluation dataset/runner and live credentials are not present at initialization;
19: model/prompt changes fail closed until approved, replayable evidence exists.
20: Feature acceptance tests, mutation checks and performance results are not claimed.
21: 
22: ## D eligibility-gate test approval target
23: 
24: Before D application code, a non-D reviewer must approve the tests-only change as
25: described in [the shared GitHub Flow](../testing/test-approval-process.md). The
26: fixed negative matrix in `test/offline/test_eligibility.py` must include analyst
27: not-run/failure, absent/unknown/unavailable evidence, missing/malformed/future/
28: stale snapshot dates, invalid rating, multiple simultaneous failures, and a model
29: `Buy` conflicting with each blocked-evidence case. Expected ratings, reason-code
30: ordering and user-visible status are literals in tests, independent of production
31: helpers. Integration cases must assert graph output, CLI, Markdown/HTML, state-log
32: authority and exclusion of `REVIEW` from pending settlement/reflection. At least
33: one valid-rating/evidence case proves the gate permits eligible results; standard
34: mode proves baseline behavior is preserved. NFR-D passes only when the fixed
35: negative set reports zero actionable outputs and zero REVIEW settlement entries.
36: 
37: The proposal reuses the existing 10-calendar-day Yahoo OHLCV stale-data guard;
38: the tests pin 10 days as accepted and 11 days as stale. If ADR review changes this
39: boundary, revise and reapprove the tests before writing application code.
40: 
41: Record the baseline before moving packages and the migrated suite afterward.
42: Initialization authorizes structural path changes only. CI bootstrap checks do not
43: prove every D7 gate or remote branch protection is already operational.

</content>

1: # D eligibility-gate test plan
2: 
3: Status: tests-only plan prepared; independent non-D test approval is pending.
4: 
5: ## Trace and scope
6: 
7: - Requirements: FR-D, NFR-D.
8: - Invariant/decision: INV-D, ADR-002.
9: - Owner: D. Safety acceptance reviewer: a team member other than D.
10: - Offline suite: `test/offline/test_eligibility.py`; no model API, market API,
11:   account input, or live credential is used.
12: - The application implementation is explicitly outside this tests-only stage.
13: 
14: ## Candidate public evaluator contract
15: 
16: `tradingagents.enhancements.eligibility.evaluate_eligibility(...)` accepts
17: `decision_mode="team"`, a candidate rating, a market-analyst execution state
18: (`completed`, `not_run`, or `failed`), market-evidence state (`valid`, `not_run`,
19: or `unavailable`), optional snapshot date, and analysis date. It returns an immutable decision with
20: `final_rating`, `eligible`, ordered `reason_codes`, and a deterministic
21: `user_message`. Unknown/missing states and malformed dates fail closed. This is a
22: proposal for test review, not an implemented interface.
23: 
24: The exact valid rating values are `Buy`, `Overweight`, `Hold`, `Underweight`,
25: `Sell`. Valid evidence requires a valid ISO calendar date no later than the
26: analysis date and no more than 10 calendar days earlier. The 10-day limit reuses
27: the current upstream `MAX_OHLCV_STALE_DAYS`; tests cover its inclusive boundary.
28: 
29: Proposed reason precedence (all applicable reasons, fixed order):
30: 
31: 1. `market_analyst_not_run`, `market_analyst_failed`, or
32:    `market_analyst_invalid_status`.
33: 2. `market_evidence_missing`, `market_evidence_not_run`,
34:    `market_evidence_unavailable`, or `market_evidence_invalid_status`.
35: 3. `market_snapshot_date_missing`, `market_snapshot_date_invalid`,
36:    `market_snapshot_after_analysis`, or `market_snapshot_stale` (date checks
37:    apply when evidence status is `valid`).
38: 4. `analysis_date_invalid`.
39: 5. `invalid_rating`.
40: 
41: The evaluator returns the candidate rating unchanged only when it is in the
42: allowlist and all evidence preconditions pass. Otherwise it returns exactly
43: `REVIEW`; human-visible message must state that review is required and name the
44: triggering conditions. Tests assert reason codes and final ratings directly,
45: without calling production helpers to construct expected values.
46: 
47: ## Fixed cases
48: 
49: | ID | Case | Expected result |
50: |---|---|---|
51: | D-UNIT-01 | Each of the five allowed ratings with completed market analyst, valid snapshot on analysis date | Same rating; eligible; no reason codes |
52: | D-UNIT-02 | Snapshot is 10 calendar days before analysis date | Same rating; eligible |
53: | D-UNIT-03 | Analyst did not run or failed | `REVIEW`; matching analyst reason |
54: | D-UNIT-04 | Evidence object missing, not run, unavailable or unknown status | `REVIEW`; matching evidence reason |
55: | D-UNIT-05 | Valid evidence has missing, malformed, future or 11-day-old snapshot date | `REVIEW`; matching date reason |
56: | D-UNIT-06 | Analysis date malformed or impossible | `REVIEW`; `analysis_date_invalid` |
57: | D-UNIT-07 | Rating absent, `REVIEW`, case-mismatched, extra prose or outside the exact allowlist | `REVIEW`; `invalid_rating` |
58: | D-UNIT-08 | Analyst not run, evidence unavailable and candidate `Buy` simultaneously | `REVIEW`; all applicable reasons in fixed order |
59: | D-UNIT-09 | The analyst report/narrative says `Buy` while evidence status is unavailable | Candidate narrative does not change `REVIEW` decision |
60: | D-UNIT-10 | The D-UNIT-03–06 matrix explicitly pairs candidate `Buy` with one analyst, evidence or date failure at a time | Each of the 16 variants returns `REVIEW` and exactly its own reason code |
61: | D-INT-01 | Team mode runs graph with valid evidence from the preceding trading day and a model rating of `Overweight` | Graph returns authoritative `Overweight`, completed/valid market statuses, the actual snapshot date, and an empty reason list |
62: | D-INT-02 | Team mode has unavailable market evidence while the model returns `Buy` | Final graph output is `REVIEW`; no actionable candidate text is exposed as final decision |
63: | D-INT-03 | Team mode runs with market analyst unselected | Final graph output is `REVIEW` with `market_analyst_not_run`; no pending settlement entry is created |
64: | D-INT-04 | Standard mode | Existing upstream result path is preserved |
65: | D-STREAM-01 | Real team-mode graph stream with unavailable evidence and a scripted PM `Buy` | No yielded decision or message exposes the rejected candidate, and at least one state publishes `REVIEW` with the reason |
66: | D-STREAM-02 | Inject an intermediate candidate `Buy` chunk into the CLI stream before the gated `REVIEW` chunk | No live decision panel contains `Buy`, and the last panel and completion notice show `REVIEW` |
67: | D-OUT-01 | Ineligible graph state is written as Markdown and HTML | Both show `REVIEW` and user-visible trigger reasons; neither shows candidate rating as final |
68: | D-OUT-02 | CLI exposes `--decision-mode standard|team`, defaulting to `standard` | Mode reaches analysis config; invalid mode is rejected |
69: | D-OUT-03 | CLI analysis completes with an ineligible final state, without opting to print the full report | Completion notice shows `REVIEW` and the same user-visible trigger reasons |
70: | D-OUT-04 | CLI's final report display receives ineligible final state | CLI display shows `REVIEW` and the same user-visible trigger reasons |
71: | D-OUT-05 | Invoke the CLI command with `--decision-mode team` and run analysis setup | `TradingAgentsGraph` construction receives `decision_mode="team"` |
72: | D-LOG-01 | State log receives ineligible final state | Stored authoritative rating/reasons are `REVIEW`/gate reasons |
73: | D-MEM-01 | A `REVIEW` result is recorded | No pending settlement/reflection entry is created |
74: 
75: ## NFR-D measurement
76: 
77: Use the independent negative evaluator cases (D-UNIT-03–08 and D-UNIT-10,
78: counting the D-UNIT-03–06 matrix once), graph cases (D-INT-02–03), and stream
79: cases (D-STREAM-01–02) as the bypass denominator.
80: Count a bypass if a blocked case produces any allowed final rating in graph,
81: CLI, Markdown, HTML or state log, or creates a pending settlement/reflection
82: entry. Acceptance requires **0 bypasses**. The tests are deterministic and CI
83: must run them on every applicable change.

110: ## PR #2 review correction

199:         this so ``--checkpoint`` actually resumes (#1249); previously the setup
200:         lived only inside ``propagate`` and the CLI streamed the checkpointer-less
201:         graph, making the flag a no-op.
202:         """
203:         self._resuming = False
204:         if not self.config.get("checkpoint_enabled"):
205:             return None
206:         signature = self._run_signature(asset_type, portfolio)
207:         self._checkpointer_ctx = get_checkpointer(self.config["data_cache_dir"], company_name)
208:         saver = self._checkpointer_ctx.__enter__()
209:         self.graph = self.workflow.compile(checkpointer=saver)
210: 
211:         step = checkpoint_step(
212:             self.config["data_cache_dir"], company_name, str(trade_date), signature
213:         )
214:         self._resuming = step is not None
215:         if step is not None:
216:             logger.info("Resuming from step %d for %s on %s", step, company_name, trade_date)
217:         else:
218:             logger.info("Starting fresh for %s on %s", company_name, trade_date)
219:         return thread_id(company_name, str(trade_date), signature)
220: 
221:     def checkpoint_input(self, init_state):
222:         """The value to stream/invoke: ``None`` to resume an existing checkpoint,
223:         else the initial state for a fresh run.
224: 
225:         LangGraph resumes an interrupted thread when invoked with ``None``;
226:         re-passing the initial state instead appends it through the message
227:         reducer, duplicating messages in the resumed state (#1249).
228:         """
229:         return None if self._resuming else init_state
230: 
231:     def end_checkpoint(self):
232:         """Restore the plain uncheckpointed graph after a checkpointed run."""
233:         if self._checkpointer_ctx is not None:
234:             self._checkpointer_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
235:             self._checkpointer_ctx = None
236:             self.graph = self.workflow.compile()
237:         self._resuming = False
238: 
239:     @contextmanager
240:     def checkpoint_scope(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = "stock", portfolio=None):
241:         """Context-manager form of begin/end_checkpoint for the propagate path."""
242:         try:
243:             yield self.begin_checkpoint(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)
244:         finally:
245:             self.end_checkpoint()
246: 
247:     def clear_checkpoint_on_success(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = "stock", portfolio=None):
248:         """Drop a completed run's checkpoint so a later run starts fresh (#1249)."""
249:         if self.config.get("checkpoint_enabled"):
250:             clear_checkpoint(
251:                 self.config["data_cache_dir"], company_name, str(trade_date),
252:                 self._run_signature(asset_type, portfolio),
253:             )
254: 
255:     def run_settings(self) -> dict:
256:         """What produces this graph's runs, for the saved report and state log.
257: 
258:         An allowlist: endpoints (a backend_url can carry credentials), keys and
259:         local paths are never recorded.
260:         """
261:         cfg = self.config
262:         return {
263:             "version": tradingagents.__version__,
264:             "llm_provider": cfg.get("llm_provider"),
265:             "deep_think_provider": tier_provider(cfg, "deep") if cfg.get("llm_provider") else None,
266:             "deep_think_llm": cfg.get("deep_think_llm"),
267:             "quick_think_provider": tier_provider(cfg, "quick") if cfg.get("llm_provider") else None,
268:             "quick_think_llm": cfg.get("quick_think_llm"),
269:             "analysts": list(self.selected_analysts),
270:             "max_debate_rounds": cfg.get("max_debate_rounds"),
271:             "max_risk_discuss_rounds": cfg.get("max_risk_discuss_rounds"),
272:             "output_language": cfg.get("output_language"),
273:             "data_vendors": dict(cfg.get("data_vendors") or {}),
274:             "tool_vendors": dict(cfg.get("tool_vendors") or {}),
275:         }
276: 
277:     def save_reports(self, final_state, ticker, save_path=None, html=True) -> Path:
278:         """Write the report tree for a completed run, like the CLI does.
279: 
280:         Programmatic callers get the same on-disk reports the CLI produces. Pass
281:         an explicit ``save_path`` or let it default under ``results_dir``; the
282:         report is also written as one HTML page unless ``html`` is False.
283:         """
284:         if save_path is None:
285:             save_path = self.default_report_path(ticker)
286:         return write_report_tree(final_state, ticker, save_path, settings=self.run_settings(), html=html)
287: 
288:     def default_report_path(self, ticker) -> Path:
289:         """Where a run's reports go unless told otherwise: under results_dir, stamped now."""
290:         stamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
291:         return Path(self.config["results_dir"]) / "reports" / f"{safe_ticker_component(ticker)}_{stamp}"
292: 
293:     def create_run_state(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = "stock", portfolio=None):
294:         """Build a run's initial state; propagate() and the CLI both start here.
295: 
296:         Injects the resolved instrument identity for every agent (#814). The
297:         memory log's lessons are not here: the graph's Memory Log step settles
298:         and loads them alongside the analysts (see ``_memory_step``).
299:         """
300:         trade_date = _validate_trade_date(trade_date)
301:         return self.propagator.create_initial_state(
302:             company_name,
303:             trade_date,
304:             asset_type=asset_type,
305:             instrument_context=self.resolve_instrument_context(company_name, asset_type, trade_date),
306:             portfolio_context=portfolio.render(company_name) if portfolio is not None else "",
307:         )
308: 
309:     def _memory_step(self, state):
310:         """The graph's Memory Log step, alongside the analysts (#1428): settle every
311:         ticker's due decisions (#1445), then return the lessons known by the
312:         trade date for the Portfolio Manager (#1251).
313: 
314:         Settling fetches prices and asks the model for a reflection per decision,
315:         so it runs beside the analysts instead of before them. A failure here
316:         does not end the run: the analysts' work is kept, the lessons already in
317:         the log are used, and the report says what could not be settled.
318:         """
319:         note = ""
320:         try:
321:             # Another run settling the same log does the work; this one goes on.
322:             done = self.settle_all_pending(wait=False)
323:             if done.failed:
324:                 note = (f"{len(done.failed)} past decision(s) could not be settled this run "
325:                         "and stay pending.")
326:         except Exception as exc:
327:             logger.warning("Settling past decisions failed: %s", exc)
328:             note = f"Past decisions could not be settled this run ({type(exc).__name__}); they stay pending."
329:         try:
330:             past_context = self.memory_log.get_past_context(
331:                 state["company_of_interest"], as_of=self._memory_as_of(state["trade_date"]))
332:         except Exception as exc:
333:             logger.warning("Reading the memory log failed: %s", exc)
334:             past_context = ""
335:             note = note or f"The memory log could not be read this run ({type(exc).__name__})."
336:         return {"past_context": past_context, "memory_note": note}
337: 
338:     def settle_pending(self, company_name) -> settlement.Settlement:
339:         """Settle this ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded.
340: 
341:         A run settles every due decision alongside its analysts, so its own
342:         decision stays pending until a later run. A caller that is done
343:         analyzing a ticker (a backtest sweep, a scheduled job) calls this to
344:         settle it now. Returns what was settled and what failed.
345:         """
346:         with run_config(self.config):
347:             return settlement.settle_pending(company_name, self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config)
348: 
349:     def settle_all_pending(self, wait: bool = True) -> settlement.Settlement:
350:         """Settle every ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded (#1445).
351: 
352:         For a scheduler whose tickers rotate: a ticker it stops analysing would
353:         otherwise keep its decisions pending, and their lessons out of later runs.
354:         With ``wait=False`` a pass already running on the same log is not waited for.
355:         """
356:         with run_config(self.config):
357:             return settlement.settle_all_pending(self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config, wait=wait)
358: 
359:     def record_decision(self, company_name, trade_date, final_state):
360:         """Record a finished run: its state log, and its decision in the memory log
361:         for reflection on the next same-ticker run. propagate() and the CLI both end here."""
362:         self._log_state(trade_date, final_state)
363:         decision = final_state.get("final_trade_decision")
364:         if not decision:
365:             logger.warning("No final decision for %s on %s; nothing added to the memory log",
366:                            company_name, trade_date)
367:             return
368:         self.memory_log.store_decision(
369:             ticker=company_name, trade_date=trade_date, final_trade_decision=decision,
370:             rating=run_rating(final_state),
371:         )
372: 
373:     def _run_graph(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = "stock",
374:                    checkpoint_thread_id: str | None = None, portfolio=None):
375:         """Execute the graph and write the resulting state to disk and memory log."""
376:         init_agent_state = self.create_run_state(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)
377:         args = self.propagator.get_graph_args()
378: 
379:         # Inject the checkpoint thread_id (from checkpoint_scope) so the same
380:         # ticker+date+graph-shape resumes; a different one starts fresh (#1089).
381:         if checkpoint_thread_id is not None:
382:             args.setdefault("config", {}).setdefault("configurable", {})["thread_id"] = checkpoint_thread_id
383: 
384:         # None resumes an existing checkpoint; init_agent_state starts fresh (#1249).
385:         graph_input = self.checkpoint_input(init_agent_state)
386:         if self.debug:
387:             # A state repeats the messages before it, so each prints once (#1027).
388:             final_state, printed = {}, set()
389:             for messages, state in self.stream_run(graph_input, **args):
390:                 for msg in messages:
391:                     key = getattr(msg, "id", None) or (type(msg).__name__, getattr(msg, "content", None))
392:                     if key not in printed:
393:                         printed.add(key)
394:                         msg.pretty_print()
395:                 if state is not None:
396:                     final_state.update(state)
397:         else:
398:             final_state = self.graph.invoke(graph_input, **args)
399: 
400:         self.record_decision(company_name, trade_date, final_state)
401: 
402:         # Clear checkpoint on successful completion to avoid stale state.
403:         self.clear_checkpoint_on_success(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)
404: 
405:         return final_state, run_rating(final_state)
406: 
407:     def stream_run(self, graph_input, **args):
408:         """Stream a run as ``(messages, state)`` pairs.
409: 
410:         ``messages`` are the agents' messages, the analysts' included. ``state``
411:         is the run's state after a top-level step; for a step inside an analyst's
412:         graph it is that analyst's report once filed, else None.
413: 
414:         Each analyst works in a graph of its own, and the run's state takes the
415:         analysts' reports only when the slowest has finished, so their messages
416:         and reports come from their own finished steps ("tasks") as they happen.
417:         """
418:         args = {**args, "stream_mode": ["values", "tasks"]}
419:         # The graph's own config serves every tool call, as in propagate(), even
420:         # when the process-wide config has changed since. Each step runs in the
421:         # run's context, so the caller keeps its own between steps.
422:         context = run_config_context(self.config)
423:         stream = context.run(self.graph.stream, graph_input, subgraphs=True, **args)
424:         try:
425:             while (step := context.run(next, stream, None)) is not None:
426:                 namespace, mode, chunk = step
427:                 if namespace:
428:                     result = chunk.get("result") if mode == "tasks" else None
429:                     if isinstance(result, dict):
430:                         report = {k: v for k, v in result.items() if k != "messages" and v}
431:                         if result.get("messages") or report:
432:                             yield result.get("messages", []), report or None
433:                 elif mode == "values":
434:                     yield chunk.get("messages", []), chunk
435:         finally:
436:             context.run(stream.close)
437: 
438:     def _log_state(self, trade_date, final_state):
439:         """Write a run's final state to JSON under the run's own ticker."""
440:         entry = {
441:             "company_of_interest": final_state["company_of_interest"],
442:             "trade_date": final_state["trade_date"],
443:             "market_report": final_state["market_report"],
444:             "sentiment_report": final_state["sentiment_report"],
445:             "news_report": final_state["news_report"],

447:             "investment_debate_state": {
448:                 "bull_history": final_state["investment_debate_state"]["bull_history"],
449:                 "bear_history": final_state["investment_debate_state"]["bear_history"],
450:                 "history": final_state["investment_debate_state"]["history"],
451:                 "current_response": final_state["investment_debate_state"][
452:                     "current_response"
453:                 ],
454:             },
455:             "trader_investment_plan": final_state["trader_investment_plan"],
456:             "risk_debate_state": {
457:                 "aggressive_history": final_state["risk_debate_state"]["aggressive_history"],
458:                 "conservative_history": final_state["risk_debate_state"]["conservative_history"],
459:                 "neutral_history": final_state["risk_debate_state"]["neutral_history"],

461:             },
462:             "investment_plan": final_state["investment_plan"],
463:             "final_trade_decision": final_state["final_trade_decision"],
464:             "final_rating": run_rating(final_state),
465:             "run_settings": self.run_settings(),
466:         }
467: 
468:         # A ticker that would escape the results directory is rejected.
469:         safe_ticker = safe_ticker_component(final_state["company_of_interest"])
470:         directory = Path(self.config["results_dir"]) / safe_ticker / "TradingAgentsStrategy_logs"
471:         directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

473:         log_path = directory / f"full_states_log_{trade_date}.json"
474:         with open(log_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
475:             # Reports can be in any language and this file is read by a person.
476:             json.dump(entry, f, indent=4, ensure_ascii=False)

48: def _tools_or_done(state) -> str:
49:     """Route an analyst's turn: run its tool calls, or finish with its report."""
50:     return "tools" if state["messages"][-1].tool_calls else END
51: 
52: 
53: def _analyst_graph(spec, agent, max_tool_rounds: int):
54:     """One analyst as a graph of its own: the model and its tools, on a private message history.
55: 
56:     It returns only its report, so analysts running side by side never write the
57:     same key, and its tool calls never reach the other analysts' messages. After
58:     ``max_tool_rounds`` rounds of tool calls it is told to write its report, and
59:     that turn ends it whatever it answers, so a model that keeps calling tools
60:     cannot run the graph into its recursion limit (#1420).
61:     """
62:     output = TypedDict(f"{spec.key.capitalize()}Report", {spec.report_key: str})
63:     graph = StateGraph(AgentState, output_schema=output)
64:     graph.add_node("agent", agent)
65:     graph.add_edge(START, "agent")
66:     if not spec.tools:
67:         graph.add_edge("agent", END)
68:         return graph.compile()
69: 
70:     def calls(messages):
71:         return [call["name"] for m in messages for call in (getattr(m, "tool_calls", None) or [])]
72: 
73:     def rounds(messages) -> int:
74:         return sum(1 for m in messages if getattr(m, "tool_calls", None))
75: 
76:     def more_or_wrap_up(state) -> str:
77:         return "wrap_up" if rounds(state["messages"]) >= max_tool_rounds else "agent"
78: 
79:     def wrap_up(state):
80:         repeated = ", ".join(f"{name} x{n}" for name, n in Counter(calls(state["messages"])).most_common())
81:         logger.warning("%s used its %d tool rounds (%s); asking for its report",
82:                        spec.agent_node, max_tool_rounds, repeated)
83:         return agent({**state, "messages": [*state["messages"], HumanMessage(WRAP_UP)]})
84: 
85:     graph.add_node("tools", ToolNode(list(spec.tools)))
86:     graph.add_node("wrap_up", wrap_up)
87:     graph.add_conditional_edges("agent", _tools_or_done, ["tools", END])
88:     graph.add_conditional_edges("tools", more_or_wrap_up, ["agent", "wrap_up"])
89:     graph.add_edge("wrap_up", END)
90:     return graph.compile()
91:

93: class GraphSetup:
94:     """Handles the setup and configuration of the agent graph."""

109:     def setup_graph(

111:     ):
112:         """Set up and compile the agent workflow graph.
113: 
114:         Args:
115:             selected_analysts (list): List of analyst types to include. Options are:
116:                 - "market": Market analyst
117:                 - "social": Sentiment analyst
118:                 - "news": News analyst
119:                 - "fundamentals": Fundamentals analyst
120:             memory_node: Node that settles past decisions and returns the run's
121:                 ``past_context``. It runs alongside the analysts.
122:         """
123:         plan = build_analyst_execution_plan(selected_analysts)
124: 
125:         analyst_factories = {
126:             "market": lambda: create_market_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),
127:             "social": lambda: create_sentiment_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),
128:             "news": lambda: create_news_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),
129:             "fundamentals": lambda: create_fundamentals_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),
130:         }
131: 
132:         bull_researcher_node = create_bull_researcher(self.quick_thinking_llm)
133:         bear_researcher_node = create_bear_researcher(self.quick_thinking_llm)
134:         research_manager_node = create_research_manager(self.deep_thinking_llm)
135:         trader_node = create_trader(self.quick_thinking_llm)
136: 
137:         aggressive_analyst = create_aggressive_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)
138:         neutral_analyst = create_neutral_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)
139:         conservative_analyst = create_conservative_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)
140:         portfolio_manager_node = create_portfolio_manager(self.deep_thinking_llm)
141: 
142:         workflow = StateGraph(AgentState)
143: 
144:         for spec in plan.specs:
145:             workflow.add_node(spec.agent_node,
146:                               _analyst_graph(spec, analyst_factories[spec.key](), self.max_tool_rounds))
147: 
148:         workflow.add_node("Bull Researcher", bull_researcher_node)
149:         workflow.add_node("Bear Researcher", bear_researcher_node)

154:         workflow.add_node("Conservative Analyst", conservative_analyst)
155:         workflow.add_node("Portfolio Manager", portfolio_manager_node)
156: 
157:         # The analysts work at the same time; the research debate starts once
158:         # every one of them has filed its report. The memory log settles past
159:         # decisions alongside them: only the Portfolio Manager reads its lessons.
160:         first_steps = [spec.agent_node for spec in plan.specs]
161:         if memory_node is not None:
162:             workflow.add_node("Memory Log", memory_node)
163:             first_steps.append("Memory Log")
164:         for node in first_steps:
165:             workflow.add_edge(START, node)
166:         workflow.add_edge(first_steps, "Bull Researcher")
167: 
168:         # Both research-debate edges share the complete DEBATE_PATH_MAP (#1088).
169:         for debate_node in ("Bull Researcher", "Bear Researcher"):

179:             workflow.add_conditional_edges(

182:                 RISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP,
183:             )

<type>file</type>
<content>
1: """Settling past decisions: once a decision's holding window has traded, score
2: it against its benchmark and record a reflection on it in the memory log."""
3: 
4: import logging
5: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
6: from datetime import datetime, timedelta
7: 
8: import pandas as pd
9: 
10: from tradingagents.dataflows.symbols import normalize_symbol
11: from tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.yahoo.market import get_closes
12: 
13: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
14: 
15: 
16: def resolve_benchmark(ticker: str, config: dict) -> str:
17:     """Pick the benchmark ticker for alpha calculation against ``ticker``.
18: 
19:     ``config["benchmark_ticker"]`` overrides everything when set; otherwise
20:     the suffix map matches the ticker's exchange suffix (e.g. ``.T`` for
21:     Tokyo). US-listed tickers without a dotted suffix fall through to the
22:     empty-suffix entry (SPY by default). Unrecognised suffixes, including
23:     US tickers with dots like ``BRK.B``, also take the empty-suffix entry.
24:     Returns are compared as percentages, each in its own currency.
25:     """
26: 
27:     explicit = config.get("benchmark_ticker")
28:     if explicit:
29:         # Same alias mapping as the analyzed ticker; an unmapped alias finds
30:         # no prices, and the decision would stay pending for good.
31:         return normalize_symbol(explicit)
32:     benchmark_map = config.get("benchmark_map", {})
33:     ticker_upper = normalize_symbol(ticker)
34:     for suffix, benchmark in benchmark_map.items():
35:         if suffix and ticker_upper.endswith(suffix.upper()):
36:             return benchmark
37:     return benchmark_map.get("", "SPY")
38: 
39: 
40: def _now() -> pd.Timestamp:
41:     return pd.Timestamp.now(tz="UTC")
42: 
43: 
44: def _by_day(closes):
45:     """Final closes keyed by the calendar day of their bar, missing closes dropped.
46: 
47:     Yahoo stamps a daily bar at midnight in its market's time zone (UTC for a
48:     coin, New York for SPY), so two series meet on their dates, not their
49:     instants. A missing or non-positive close is no price at all, not a bar to
50:     score on. Today's bar, in its market's time zone, is the session still
51:     trading: its close is the live price, so it is not scored.
52:     """
53:     closes = closes[closes > 0]
54:     tz = getattr(closes.index, "tz", None)
55:     if not closes.empty:
56:         closes = closes[closes.index.date < _now().tz_convert(tz).date()]
57:     return closes if tz is None else closes.tz_localize(None)
58: 
59: 
60: def fetch_returns(
61:     ticker: str, trade_date: str, holding_days: int = 5,
62:     benchmark: str = "SPY",
63: ) -> tuple[float | None, float | None, int | None, str | None]:
64:     """Fetch raw and alpha return for ticker over holding_days after trade_date.
65: 
66:     The position is entered at the first close after ``trade_date``: a run dated
67:     ``trade_date`` reads news published after that day's close (#1518).
68: 
69:     ``benchmark`` is the index used as the alpha baseline (resolved by the
70:     caller via ``resolve_benchmark``). Returns ``(raw_return, alpha_return,
71:     holding_days, resolution_date)`` — where ``resolution_date`` is the date
72:     of the last price bar used, i.e. when the outcome became known (#1251) —
73:     or ``(None, None, None, None)`` when the full holding window has not traded
74:     yet (#1169). A failure to get or read the prices is raised, for the caller
75:     to report.
76:     """
77:     start = datetime.strptime(trade_date, "%Y-%m-%d")
78:     today = _now().tz_localize(None).normalize()
79:     # The entry and holding_days more sessions all close after the decision date
80:     # and before today, with a day's slack for markets east of UTC: until then
81:     # the window cannot have traded and no prices are asked for.
82:     if (today - start).days < holding_days + 1:
83:         return None, None, None, None
84:     # holding_days counts trading days after the entry session, so ask for the
85:     # calendar span they occupy (about 7 for every 5) plus a week for holidays.
86:     end = start + timedelta(days=round((holding_days + 1) * 7 / 5) + 7)
87:     # From a week earlier, so the benchmark has a close on or before entry.
88:     bench_start = (start - timedelta(days=7)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
89: 
90:     def closes(until):
91:         # Closes for the instrument the analysis priced (XAUUSD -> GC=F, #984),
92:         # from the first session after the decision date.
93:         stock = _by_day(get_closes(ticker, trade_date, until.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")))
94:         return stock[stock.index > start], _by_day(get_closes(benchmark, bench_start, until.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")))
95: 
96:     def traded(stock, bench):
97:         return len(stock) > holding_days and not bench.empty and bench.index[-1] >= stock.index[holding_days]
98: 
99:     stock, bench = closes(end)
100:     # A window that has passed without trading through spans a closure longer than
101:     # the week allowed for holidays (a national holiday, a halt): ask through today.
102:     if not traded(stock, bench) and end < today:
103:         stock, bench = closes(today + timedelta(days=1))
104: 
105:     # Require the full holding window to have traded. A rerun before it has
106:     # leaves the entry pending to retry next run, rather than settling on a
107:     # premature partial return (#1169).
108:     if len(stock) <= holding_days:
109:         return None, None, None, None
110:     entry, exit_ = stock.index[0], stock.index[holding_days]
111:     # The window is the stock's own sessions; the benchmark is valued at its
112:     # last close by each end, so both returns span the same dates even when
113:     # the calendars differ (a coin trades at weekends, an index does not).
114:     # It must have traded through the exit, or its close there may yet move.
115:     if bench.empty or bench.index[0] > entry or bench.index[-1] < exit_:
116:         return None, None, None, None
117: 
118:     raw = float((stock.iloc[holding_days] - stock.iloc[0]) / stock.iloc[0])
119:     bench_entry, bench_exit = bench.asof(entry), bench.asof(exit_)
120:     bench_ret = float((bench_exit - bench_entry) / bench_entry)
121:     alpha = raw - bench_ret
122:     # Every close used is known by the exit: the point-in-time cutoff for
123:     # injecting the lesson (#1251).
124:     resolution_date = exit_.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
125:     return raw, alpha, holding_days, resolution_date
126: 
127: 
128: @dataclass
129: class Settlement:
130:     """What a settlement pass did: the decisions it settled and those it could not."""
131: 
132:     settled: list[tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)        # (ticker, date)
133:     failed: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)    # (ticker, date, reason)
134: 
135: 
136: def settle_pending(ticker: str, memory_log, reflector, config: dict, wait: bool = True) -> Settlement:
137:     """Settle ``ticker``'s pending decisions whose holding window has traded.
138: 
139:     One pass at a time per log (``memory_log.settling()``), so runs sharing a log
140:     never pay for the same reflection twice. Each outcome is written as soon as
141:     its reflection is done, so an interrupted pass keeps what it finished.
142:     Entries whose window has not traded yet are skipped; an entry whose prices
143:     or reflection could not be had stays pending and is reported as failed.
144:     With ``wait=False`` a pass already running elsewhere is left to do the work.
145:     """
146:     result = Settlement()
147:     with memory_log.settling(wait=wait) as held:
148:         if not held:
149:             return result
150:         pending = [e for e in memory_log.get_pending_entries() if e["ticker"] == ticker]
151:         if not pending:
152:             return result
153:         benchmark = resolve_benchmark(ticker, config)
154:         for entry in pending:
155:             try:
156:                 raw, alpha, days, resolution_date = fetch_returns(
157:                     ticker, entry["date"], config.get("holding_period_days", 5), benchmark=benchmark,
158:                 )
159:             except Exception as exc:
160:                 logger.warning("Prices for settling %s on %s were unavailable: %s", ticker, entry["date"], exc)
161:                 result.failed.append((ticker, entry["date"], f"prices unavailable: {exc}"))
162:                 continue
163:             if raw is None:
164:                 continue  # the holding window has not traded yet: try again next run
165:             try:
166:                 reflection = reflector.reflect_on_final_decision(
167:                     final_decision=entry.get("decision", ""),
168:                     raw_return=raw,
169:                     alpha_return=alpha,
170:                     benchmark_name=benchmark,
171:                     holding_days=days,
172:                 )
173:             except Exception as exc:
174:                 # Reflection calls a provider: a transient failure leaves the entry
175:                 # pending for the next pass rather than stopping the analysis.
176:                 logger.warning("Reflection failed for %s on %s: %s", ticker, entry["date"], exc)
177:                 result.failed.append((ticker, entry["date"], f"reflection failed: {exc}"))
178:                 continue
179:             if memory_log.update_with_outcome(ticker, entry["date"], raw, alpha, days, reflection,
180:                                               resolution_date=resolution_date):
181:                 result.settled.append((ticker, entry["date"]))
182:     return result
183: 
184: 
185: def settle_all_pending(memory_log, reflector, config: dict, wait: bool = True) -> Settlement:
186:     """Settle every ticker's pending decisions whose holding window has traded (#1445).
187: 
188:     A run settles its own ticker; a ticker no longer analysed would otherwise
189:     keep its decisions pending, and their lessons out of later runs.
190:     """
191:     result = Settlement()
192:     for ticker in dict.fromkeys(e["ticker"] for e in memory_log.get_pending_entries()):
193:         done = settle_pending(ticker, memory_log, reflector, config, wait=wait)
194:         result.settled.extend(done.settled)
195:         result.failed.extend(done.failed)
196:     return result

</content>

1: """Reusable report-tree writer shared by the CLI and the programmatic API.
2: 
3: Writes a run's per-section markdown (analysts, research, trading, risk,
4: portfolio) plus a consolidated ``complete_report.md`` under ``save_path``. The
5: CLI and ``TradingAgentsGraph.save_reports`` both call this, so a headless / API
6: run produces the same on-disk report tree a CLI run does.
7: """
8: 
9: from datetime import datetime
10: from pathlib import Path
11: 
12: from tradingagents.agents.rating import run_rating
13: 
14: 
15: def analyst_names(keys) -> list[str]:
16:     """The analysts as users select them: the sentiment analyst's key is "social"."""
17:     return ["sentiment" if key == "social" else key for key in keys or []]
18: 
19: 
20: def _header(ticker: str, final_state: dict, settings: dict | None) -> str:
21:     """The report's title and what produced it: analysis date, version, models, analysts, vendors."""
22:     lines = [f"# Trading Analysis Report: {ticker}", ""]
23:     if final_state.get("trade_date"):
24:         lines.append(f"- Analysis date: {final_state['trade_date']}")
25:     if final_state.get("final_trade_decision"):
26:         lines.append(f"- Rating: {run_rating(final_state)}")
27:     lines.append(f"- Generated: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}")
28:     if settings:
29:         s = settings.get
30:         deep_provider = s("deep_think_provider") or s("llm_provider", "?")
31:         quick_provider = s("quick_think_provider") or s("llm_provider", "?")
32:         if deep_provider == quick_provider:
33:             models = f"{deep_provider}, deep {s('deep_think_llm', '?')}, quick {s('quick_think_llm', '?')}"
34:         else:   # each tier on its own provider (#1440)
35:             models = (f"deep {deep_provider} {s('deep_think_llm', '?')}, "
36:                       f"quick {quick_provider} {s('quick_think_llm', '?')}")
37:         lines.append(f"- TradingAgents {s('version', '?')}: {models}")
38:         lines.append(f"- Analysts: {', '.join(analyst_names(s('analysts')))}; "
39:                      f"research debate rounds {s('max_debate_rounds', '?')}, "
40:                      f"risk debate rounds {s('max_risk_discuss_rounds', '?')}")
41:         vendors = {**(s("data_vendors") or {}), **(s("tool_vendors") or {})}
42:         if vendors:
43:             lines.append("- Data vendors: " + ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in vendors.items()))
44:     if final_state.get("memory_note"):
45:         lines.append(f"- Memory log: {final_state['memory_note']}")
46:     return "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n"
47: 
48: 
49: # The report's sections in order: (heading, folder, [(agent, file, state path)]).
50: _SECTIONS = (
51:     ("I. Analyst Team Reports", "1_analysts", (
52:         ("Market Analyst", "market.md", ("market_report",)),
53:         ("Sentiment Analyst", "sentiment.md", ("sentiment_report",)),
54:         ("News Analyst", "news.md", ("news_report",)),
55:         ("Fundamentals Analyst", "fundamentals.md", ("fundamentals_report",)),
56:     )),
57:     ("II. Research Team Decision", "2_research", (
58:         ("Bull Researcher", "bull.md", ("investment_debate_state", "bull_history")),
59:         ("Bear Researcher", "bear.md", ("investment_debate_state", "bear_history")),
60:         ("Research Manager", "manager.md", ("investment_plan",)),
61:     )),
62:     ("III. Trading Team Plan", "3_trading", (
63:         ("Trader", "trader.md", ("trader_investment_plan",)),
64:     )),
65:     ("IV. Risk Management Team Decision", "4_risk", (
66:         ("Aggressive Analyst", "aggressive.md", ("risk_debate_state", "aggressive_history")),
67:         ("Conservative Analyst", "conservative.md", ("risk_debate_state", "conservative_history")),
68:         ("Neutral Analyst", "neutral.md", ("risk_debate_state", "neutral_history")),
69:     )),
70:     ("V. Portfolio Manager Decision", "5_portfolio", (
71:         ("Portfolio Manager", "decision.md", ("final_trade_decision",)),
72:     )),
73: )
74: 
75: 
76: def _report_parts(final_state: dict) -> list[tuple[str, str, list[tuple[str, str, str]]]]:
77:     """The sections with something to say: (heading, folder, [(agent, file, text)])."""
78:     parts = []
79:     for heading, folder, agents in _SECTIONS:
80:         written = []
81:         for agent, filename, path in agents:
82:             value = final_state
83:             for key in path:
84:                 value = (value or {}).get(key)
85:             if value:
86:                 written.append((agent, filename, value))
87:         if written:
88:             parts.append((heading, folder, written))
89:     return parts
90: 
91: 
92: def write_report_tree(final_state: dict, ticker: str, save_path, settings: dict | None = None,
93:                       html: bool = True) -> Path:
94:     """Save a completed run's reports to ``save_path``; return the complete-report path.
95: 
96:     ``settings`` (``TradingAgentsGraph.run_settings()``) adds what produced the run
97:     to the report's header. ``html`` also writes ``complete_report.html``, one
98:     self-contained page of the same report (#1419).
99:     Reusing a directory replaces the generated report files, removing sections
100:     absent from this run and disabled HTML. Other files and directories are kept.
101:     """
102:     save_path = Path(save_path)
103:     save_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
104:     parts = _report_parts(final_state)
105:     sections = []
106:     for heading, folder, written in parts:
107:         (save_path / folder).mkdir(exist_ok=True)
108:         for _agent, filename, text in written:
109:             (save_path / folder / filename).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
110:         content = "\n\n".join(f"### {agent}\n{text}" for agent, _filename, text in written)
111:         sections.append(f"## {heading}\n\n{content}")
112: 
113:     (save_path / "complete_report.md").write_text(
114:         _header(ticker, final_state, settings) + "\n\n".join(sections), encoding="utf-8"
115:     )
116:     if html:
117:         from tradingagents.report_html import render_report
118: 
119:         (save_path / "complete_report.html").write_text(
120:             render_report(ticker, final_state, settings, parts), encoding="utf-8"
121:         )
122:     else:
123:         (save_path / "complete_report.html").unlink(missing_ok=True)
124: 
125:     # Reconcile only the filenames owned by this writer; never clear the tree,
126:     # since callers may keep notes or other artifacts alongside the reports.
127:     current_files = {
128:         (folder, filename)
129:         for _heading, folder, written in parts
130:         for _agent, filename, _text in written
131:     }
132:     for _heading, folder, agents in _SECTIONS:
133:         for _agent, filename, _path in agents:
134:             if (folder, filename) not in current_files:
135:                 (save_path / folder / filename).unlink(missing_ok=True)
136:     return save_path / "complete_report.md"

186: 
187: def _markdown() -> MarkdownIt:
188:     md = MarkdownIt("commonmark", {"html": False}).enable("table").disable("image")
189:     md.add_render_rule("table_open", lambda *a: '<div class="table"><table>\n')
190:     md.add_render_rule("table_close", lambda *a: "</table></div>\n")
191:     return md
192: 
193: 
194: def _render_agent_text(md: MarkdownIt, text: str) -> str:
195:     """An agent's text, its own headings placed below the agent's heading (h3)."""
196:     tokens = md.parse(text)
197:     for token in tokens:
198:         if token.type in ("heading_open", "heading_close"):
199:             token.tag = f"h{min(int(token.tag[1]) + 3, 6)}"
200:     return md.renderer.render(tokens, md.options, {})
201: 
202: 
203: # What each data category serves, as a reader would name it.
204: _CATEGORY = {
205:     "core_stock_apis": "Prices", "technical_indicators": "Indicators", "fundamental_data": "Fundamentals",
206:     "news_data": "News", "macro_data": "Macro", "prediction_markets": "Prediction markets",
207: }
208: 
209: 
210: def _fields(values) -> str:
211:     return " ".join(f'<span class="field">{escape(str(v))}</span>' for v in values)
212: 
213: 
214: def _chain(vendors: str) -> str:
215:     """A vendor chain in the order it is tried: ``a,b`` reads a, then b."""
216:     names = [v.strip() for v in str(vendors).split(",") if v.strip()]
217:     return ' <span class="then">\u2192</span> '.join(_fields([n]) for n in names)
218: 
219: 
220: def _group(name: str, values_html: str) -> str:
221:     return f'<span class="group"><span class="name">{escape(name)}</span>{values_html}</span>'
222: 
223: 
224: def _run_details(final_state: dict, settings: dict | None) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
225:     """The run details as (label, value HTML); every value from the run is escaped."""
226:     details = [("Generated", escape(datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")))]
227:     if settings:
228:         s = settings.get
229:         for tier in ("deep", "quick"):
230:             provider = s(f"{tier}_think_provider") or s("llm_provider", "?")
231:             details.append((f"{tier.capitalize()} model", _fields([provider, s(f"{tier}_think_llm", "?")])))
232:         details.append(("Analysts", _fields(analyst_names(s("analysts")))))
233:         details.append(("Debate rounds", " ".join((
234:             _group("research", _fields([s("max_debate_rounds", "?")])),
235:             _group("risk", _fields([s("max_risk_discuss_rounds", "?")])),
236:         ))))
237:         vendors = {**(s("data_vendors") or {}), **(s("tool_vendors") or {})}
238:         if vendors:
239:             details.append(("Data vendors", " ".join(
240:                 _group(_CATEGORY.get(k, k), _chain(v)) for k, v in vendors.items()
241:             )))
242:         details.append(("Version", escape(f"TradingAgents {s('version', '?')}")))
243:     if final_state.get("memory_note"):
244:         details.append(("Memory log", escape(final_state["memory_note"])))
245:     return details
246: 
247: 
248: def render_report(ticker: str, final_state: dict, settings: dict | None, parts) -> str:
249:     """The report page: title and rating, what produced the run, contents, sections."""
250:     md = _markdown()
251:     rating = run_rating(final_state) if final_state.get("final_trade_decision") else ""
252:     tone = _TONE.get(rating, "review")
253:     date = final_state.get("trade_date", "")
254: 
255:     title = f'<span class="ticker">{escape(ticker)}</span>'
256:     if rating:
257:         title += f' <span class="rating {tone}">{escape(rating)}</span>'
258:     details = "".join(
259:         f'<div class="{"note" if label == "Memory log" else "detail"}">'
260:         f"<dt>{escape(label)}</dt><dd>{value}</dd></div>"
261:         for label, value in _run_details(final_state, settings)
262:     )
263: 
264:     contents, body = [], []
265:     for n, (heading, _folder, written) in enumerate(parts, 1):
266:         agents = "".join(
267:             f'<li><a href="#s{n}-{m}"><span class="bar"></span> <span class="label">{escape(agent)}</span></a></li>'
268:             for m, (agent, _f, _t) in enumerate(written, 1)
269:         )
270:         numeral, _, name = heading.partition(". ")
271:         contents.append(f'<li><a href="#s{n}"><span class="num">{escape(numeral)}</span> '
272:                         f'<span class="label">{escape(name)}</span></a><ul>{agents}</ul></li>')
273:         body.append(f'<section id="s{n}"><h2>{escape(heading)}</h2>')
274:         for m, (agent, _filename, text) in enumerate(written, 1):
275:             body.append(f'<h3 id="s{n}-{m}">{escape(agent)}</h3>\n{_render_agent_text(md, text)}')
276:         body.append("</section>")
277: 
278:     page_title = " ".join(x for x in (ticker, date, rating) if x)

<content>
1: """Shared 5-tier rating vocabulary and a deterministic heuristic parser.
2: 
3: The same five-tier scale (Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell) is used by:
4: - The Research Manager (investment plan recommendation)
5: - The Portfolio Manager (final position decision; its free-text fallback is read here)
6: - The memory log (rating tag stored alongside each decision entry)
7: 
8: Centralising it here avoids drift between those call sites.
9: 
10: ``extract_rating`` returns ``None`` when no rating can be found, and every
11: caller turns that into ``REVIEW`` rather than a tradeable position: a decision
12: nobody can read is not a Hold, and a Hold recorded in its place is quoted back to
13: the next run as a call that was never made (#1170).
14: """
15: 
16: from __future__ import annotations
17: 
18: import re
19: import unicodedata
20: 
21: # Canonical, ordered 5-tier scale (most bullish to most bearish).
22: RATINGS_5_TIER: tuple[str, ...] = (
23:     "Buy", "Overweight", "Hold", "Underweight", "Sell",
24: )
25: 
26: # Signal emitted when the model's decision has no recognizable rating. It is not
27: # a tradeable position: it flags output that needs a human/re-run rather than
28: # silently degrading to Hold. Callers that map the signal onto the 5-tier enum
29: # (e.g. ``PortfolioRating(signal)``) should guard with ``is_review`` first.
30: RATING_REVIEW = "REVIEW"
31: 
32: _RATING_SET = {r.lower() for r in RATINGS_5_TIER}
33: 
34: # Matches "Rating: X" / "rating - X" / "Rating — **X**" — tolerates markdown
35: # bold wrappers and any dash or colon a model writes as the separator. "rating"
36: # must start a word, so "Operating margin: Sell-side" is not a label.
37: _RATING_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![a-z])rating\b[^:\-\u2010-\u2015]*[:\-\u2010-\u2015][\s*]*(\w+)",
38:                               re.IGNORECASE)
39: 
40: # The decision's own rating line, in the shape the Portfolio Manager is asked to
41: # open with ("- **Rating**: X", "**Final Rating**: X", "## Our rating - X"): an
42: # optional list marker, emphasis and heading marks, and only words naming the
43: # decision itself before "rating". "Consensus rating: Buy" or "Trader's rating:
44: # Buy" is someone else's rating.
45: _OWN_QUALIFIER = r"(?:(?:final|our|overall|my|recommended|updated|revised|new|current)\s+)*"
46: _RATING_LINE_RE = re.compile(
47:     r"\s*(?P<item>(?:[-+*\u2022]|\d+[.)])\s+)?[\s*_#]*" + _OWN_QUALIFIER
48:     + r"rating[^\w:\-\u2010-\u2015]*[:\-\u2010-\u2015][\s*]*(?P<value>\w+)",
49:     re.IGNORECASE,
50: )
51: 
52: # A line presenting the scale rather than a decision ("Rating Scale: Buy, ...").
53: _RATING_SCALE_RE = re.compile(r"rating\s*(scale|options|legend)", re.IGNORECASE)
54: 
55: def extract_rating(text: str) -> str | None:
56:     """Extract a 5-tier rating from its label, or ``None`` if there is none.
57: 
58:     Reads an explicit "Rating: X" label (tolerant of markdown bold) in the
59:     NFKC-normalized text, so fullwidth punctuation like ``Rating：Overweight``
60:     matches as ASCII does: the decision's opening rating line, else its own
61:     rating lines or, failing those, every label, when they agree.
62:     """
63:     if not text:
64:         return None
65:     norm = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text)
66: 
67:     # The decision is asked to open with its rating, so a first line (after any
68:     # headings) in that shape is the call. A list item there may also be a quote
69:     # heading a list of other parties' ratings, so it counts with the decision's
70:     # other rating lines, which leave out list items; failing those, every label
71:     # counts. Either way they must agree: ratings that differ, with nothing
72:     # marking which one is the call, are no call (#1170). Lines presenting the
73:     # scale itself are a legend the model echoed, not a call.
74:     lines = [line for line in norm.splitlines() if line.strip() and not _RATING_SCALE_RE.search(line)]
75:     first = next((line for line in lines if not line.lstrip().startswith("#")
76:                   or _RATING_LINE_RE.match(line)), "")
77:     m = _RATING_LINE_RE.match(first)
78:     opening = m if m and m.group("value").lower() in _RATING_SET else None
79:     if opening and not opening.group("item"):
80:         return opening.group("value").capitalize()
81: 
82:     own = [opening.group("value").capitalize()] if opening else []
83:     labels = []
84:     for line in lines:
85:         m = _RATING_LINE_RE.match(line)
86:         if m and not m.group("item") and m.group("value").lower() in _RATING_SET:
87:             own.append(m.group("value").capitalize())
88:         labels += [v.capitalize() for v in _RATING_LABEL_RE.findall(line) if v.lower() in _RATING_SET]
89:     # Without a label there is no call to read: a rating word in the prose may be
90:     # one the text argues against ("not a Sell"), and reading it reports a
91:     # direction nobody decided.
92:     found = own or labels
93:     return found[0] if found and len(set(found)) == 1 else None
94: 
95: 
96: def parse_rating(text: str, default: str = RATING_REVIEW) -> str:
97:     """Extract a 5-tier rating, or ``REVIEW`` when the decision has none.
98: 
99:     For callers that need a string for every decision, such as the memory log's
100:     entry tag. The default is the review sentinel, never a tradeable rating.
101:     """
102:     rating = extract_rating(text)
103:     return rating if rating is not None else default
104: 
105: 
106: def run_rating(final_state: dict) -> str:
107:     """A finished run's rating: the Portfolio Manager's own, else read from its decision.
108: 
109:     The fallback serves a state without ``final_rating``, such as a run an older
110:     version completed and a checkpoint hands back unchanged.
111:     """
112:     return final_state.get("final_rating") or parse_rating(final_state.get("final_trade_decision", ""))
113: 
114: 
115: def is_review(signal: str) -> bool:
116:     """Whether a signal is the non-tradeable REVIEW sentinel (#1170)."""
117:     return signal == RATING_REVIEW

392: def _yes(question: str) -> bool:
393:     return typer.prompt(question, default="Y").strip().upper() in ("Y", "YES", "")
394: 
395: 
396: def _graphical_browser():
397:     """A browser that opens a page in its own window on this machine, or None.
398: 
399:     Over SSH the page sits on the remote machine, and a terminal browser (lynx,
400:     w3m, elinks) would take over the terminal, so neither is offered.
401:     """
402:     if os.environ.get("SSH_CONNECTION") or os.environ.get("SSH_TTY"):
403:         return None
404:     try:
405:         browser = webbrowser.get()
406:     except webbrowser.Error:
407:         return None
408:     if type(browser) is webbrowser.GenericBrowser or isinstance(browser, webbrowser.Elinks):
409:         return None
410:     return browser
411: 
412: 
413: def _open_page(page: Path) -> None:
414:     """Offer to open the saved page in a browser window, and say where it is if opening fails."""
415:     browser = _graphical_browser()
416:     if browser is None or not _yes("Open it in your browser?"):
417:         return
418:     try:
419:         opened = browser.open(page.as_uri())
420:     except (webbrowser.Error, OSError):
421:         opened = False
422:     if not opened:
423:         console.print(f"  [dim]Could not open a browser; the page is at:[/dim] {page}")
424:

426: def _offer_reports(final_state, graph, ticker, save=None, show=None, html=None):
427:     """Save the report tree and show it; ``save``/``show``/``html`` answer the questions when given.
428: 
429:     A saved report includes the HTML page unless ``html`` is False. Someone
430:     answering the save question at the prompt is also asked about the page and
431:     offered to open it; a run whose flags answer the save question asks neither.
432:     """
433:     asked = save is None
434:     if asked:
435:         save = typer.prompt("Save report?", default="Y").strip().upper() in ("Y", "YES", "")
436:     if save:
437:         # Under results_dir, not the working directory: in Docker the working
438:         # directory is inside the container and the report goes with it, while
439:         # results_dir is the mounted volume the rest of the run already writes to.
440:         save_path = graph.default_report_path(ticker)
441:         if asked:   # someone at the prompt may pick another folder
442:             save_path = Path(typer.prompt(
443:                 "Save path (press Enter for default)", default=str(save_path)
444:             ).strip())
445:         if html is None:
446:             html = _yes("Also save it as an HTML page?") if asked else True
447:         saved = False
448:         try:
449:             report_file = graph.save_reports(final_state, ticker, save_path, html=html)
450:             saved = True
451:             console.print(f"\n[green]✓ Report saved to:[/green] {save_path.resolve()}")
452:             console.print(f"  [dim]Complete report:[/dim] {report_file.name}")
453:         except Exception as e:
454:             console.print(f"[red]Error saving report: {e}[/red]")
455:         if saved and html:
456:             page = (save_path / "complete_report.html").resolve()
457:             console.print(f"  [dim]HTML report:[/dim] {page.name}")
458:             if asked:
459:                 _open_page(page)
460: 
461:     if show is None:
462:         show = typer.prompt("\nDisplay full report on screen?", default="Y").strip().upper() in ("Y", "YES", "")
463:     if show:

465: def update_analyst_statuses(message_buffer, chunk, wall_time_tracker=None):
466:     """Update analyst statuses from the reports filed so far.
467: 
468:     The analysts run together: each is in progress until its own report lands.
469:     When every selected analyst has filed, the research debate is in progress.
470:     """
471:     selected = message_buffer.selected_analysts
472: 
473:     if wall_time_tracker is not None:
474:         sync_analyst_tracker_from_chunk(wall_time_tracker, chunk)
475: 
476:     all_filed = True
477:     for analyst_key in ANALYST_ORDER:
478:         if analyst_key not in selected:
479:             continue
480: 
481:         agent_name = ANALYST_AGENT_NAMES[analyst_key]
482:         report_key = ANALYST_REPORT_MAP[analyst_key]
483: 
484:         # Capture new report content from current chunk
485:         if chunk.get(report_key):
486:             message_buffer.update_report_section(report_key, chunk[report_key])
487: 
488:         # Status comes from accumulated sections, not just the current chunk.
489:         if message_buffer.report_sections.get(report_key):
490:             message_buffer.update_agent_status(agent_name, "completed")
491:         else:
492:             message_buffer.update_agent_status(agent_name, "in_progress")
493:             all_filed = False
494: 
495:     if (
496:         all_filed
497:         and selected
498:         and message_buffer.agent_status.get("Bull Researcher") == "pending"
499:     ):
500:         message_buffer.update_agent_status("Bull Researcher", "in_progress")

502: 
503: def extract_content_string(content):
504:     """Extract string content from various message formats.
505:     Returns None if no meaningful text content is found.
506:     """
507:     def is_empty(val):
508:         """Whether a value carries nothing to show.
509: 
510:         Text is judged by whether anything was written, not by what it would
511:         mean as Python: a report saying "0" or "None" is a message the run
512:         produced, and reading it as a falsy literal dropped it from the display.
513:         """
514:         if isinstance(val, str):
515:             return not val.strip()
516:         return val is None or not bool(val)
517: 
518:     if is_empty(content):
519:         return None
520: 
521:     if isinstance(content, str):
522:         return content.strip()
523: 
524:     if isinstance(content, dict):
525:         text = content.get('text', '')
526:         return text.strip() if not is_empty(text) else None
527: 
528:     if isinstance(content, list):
529:         text_parts = [
530:             item.get('text', '').strip() if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get('type') == 'text'
531:             else (item.strip() if isinstance(item, str) else '')
532:             for item in content
533:         ]
534:         result = ' '.join(t for t in text_parts if t and not is_empty(t))
535:         return result if result else None
536: 
537:     return str(content).strip() if not is_empty(content) else None
538: 
539: 
540: def classify_message_type(message) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
541:     """Classify LangChain message into display type and extract content.
542: 
543:     Returns:
544:         (type, content) - type is one of: User, Agent, Data, Control
545:                         - content is extracted string or None
546:     """
547:     from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage, ToolMessage
548: 
549:     content = extract_content_string(getattr(message, 'content', None))
550: 
551:     if isinstance(message, HumanMessage):
552:         if content and content.strip() == "Continue":
553:             return ("Control", content)
554:         return ("User", content)
555: 
556:     if isinstance(message, ToolMessage):
557:         return ("Data", content)
558: 
559:     if isinstance(message, AIMessage):
560:         return ("Agent", content)
561: 
562:     # Fallback for unknown types
563:     return ("System", content)

566: def format_tool_args(args, max_length=80) -> str:
567:     """Format tool arguments for terminal display."""
568:     result = str(args)
569:     if len(result) > max_length:
570:         return result[:max_length - 3] + "..."
